dataSheet.description: A generic full-size pickup in the 2.4 t class with full-time four-wheel drive: roughly 220 kW, 3.7 m wheelbase, nose-heavy, high centre of mass, independent front and a leaf-sprung solid rear axle.
sources: Class-typical figures from manufacturer specification sheets for full-size pickups (kerb mass 2200–2600 kg, wheelbase 3.5–3.9 m, Cd 0.40–0.47, 56/44 front weight bias unladen, centre of mass 0.7–0.8 m).
Tire feel parameters tuned to a ~0.75 g skidpad and ~44 m 100–0 km/h braking distance on all-terrain tires, in the range of published road tests for the class.

Suspension rates for ~1.3 Hz front and ~1.5 Hz rear ride frequencies unladen (Gillespie, Fundamentals of Vehicle Dynamics, ch. 5); a leaf-sprung solid rear axle has its roll centre near the spring-seat height, about 0.4 m, and the independent front near 0.1 m (Milliken & Milliken, Race Car Vehicle Dynamics, ch. 17).

Drivetrain [ILLUSTRATIVE]: a 3.5 l V6 (peak 520 N·m at 3000 rpm, 220 kW at 5600 rpm) through a six-speed automatic with a 3.7 final drive, open axle differentials and a centre differential sending 40 % forward, as on a full-time 4WD system.

Steering geometry [ILLUSTRATIVE]: 4° of caster (about 25 mm of trail), a 20 mm scrub radius and strong hydraulic assist; aero after Hucho, Aerodynamics of Road Vehicles, ch. 4: a tall bluff body with mild lift and the drag centred well above the centre of mass.
dataSheet.notes: Not a specific production model. The rear axle is a solid beam (suspension.kind "solid", ADR-0016) with a high roll centre, so most of its lateral load transfer goes through the links and the body rolls less than the soft springs alone would allow.
